title.en: Write a Text File, Read It Back

blurb.en: One file, written once, read three different ways, then appended to - and the newline that rides along on every line.
blurb.zh: 一个文件，写一次、用三种方式读、再追加一行——外加每一行都偷偷带着的那个换行符。

en: with open(...) as f closes the file for you when the block ends, even if something inside it raises an exception. Before with existed you had to call f.close() yourself, and a file left open may not have its last writes flushed to disk. There is no good reason to open a file any other way in your own code.

The mode decides what happens to what is already there. "w" empties the file the moment it is opened - before you write a single character - so opening an existing file with "w" by mistake destroys it. "a" keeps the contents and adds to the end. Leaving the mode out means "r": read only, and an error if the file does not exist.

write() does not add a newline for you; print() does, write() does not. That is why write_lines glues one on. It also means every line you read back still carries it: the repr and readlines() output show the \n at the end of each line, and printing a line unchanged would leave a blank line after each one. Removing only that trailing newline is the tidy fix, because removing all whitespace would also eat spaces that were meant to be data.

The three ways to read: read() gives one string of the whole file; readlines() gives a list of lines; looping over the file object gives one line at a time without holding the whole file in memory, which is the one to reach for when a file might be large.
zh: with open(...) as f 会在块结束时替你关掉文件，即使块里抛了异常也一样。没有 with 的年代得自己调 f.close()，而没关的文件，最后写的那点内容可能还没真正落到磁盘上。自己的代码里没有理由用别的方式打开文件。
打开模式决定已有内容的命运。"w" 在打开的那一刻就把文件清空——你一个字符都还没写——所以错用 "w" 打开一个已有文件，就等于把它毁了。"a" 保留原内容，往末尾接。不写模式就是 "r"：只读，文件不存在就报错。
write() 不会替你加换行；print() 加，write() 不加。所以 write_lines 要自己拼一个。这也意味着读回来的每一行都还带着它：repr 与 readlines() 的输出里每行末尾都看得见 \n；原样打印一行，每行后面会多出一个空行。只去掉末尾那个换行符是干净的修法——把所有空白都去掉，会把本来属于数据的空格一起吃掉。
三种读法：read() 把整个文件读成一个字符串；readlines() 给出行的列表；直接对文件对象做循环则一次拿一行、不必把整个文件放进内存——文件可能很大时，用的就是这一种。

lineNotes.en: Mode "w" truncates on open. If shopping.txt already existed, its old contents are gone before the loop below writes anything.
lineNotes.zh: 模式 "w" 一打开就截断。shopping.txt 若原本就有，下面的循环还没写任何东西，旧内容就已经没了。

lineNotes.en: The newline is added by hand. Leave it off and all three items end up on one line: eggsmilkbread.
lineNotes.zh: 换行是手工加的。不加的话，三样东西会挤在同一行：eggsmilkbread。

lineNotes.en: This is a second open of the same file. The first with block already closed it, and a fresh open starts reading from the beginning again.
lineNotes.zh: 这是对同一个文件的第二次打开。第一个 with 块已经把它关了，重新打开就从头开始读。

title.en: Read a CSV: split by Hand

blurb.en: Read a small table of marks by stripping each line and splitting it on commas - and see exactly where that stops working.
blurb.zh: 读一张小成绩表：每行去掉换行、按逗号切开——再看清这种做法在哪里失灵。

en: The file is read in two stages. readline() takes the header row on its own, and the for loop then carries on from wherever the file currently is, so it sees only the data rows. A file object remembers its position; you do not have to skip the header inside the loop.
Every field comes back as a string, including the marks. "91" + "78" is "9178", so each mark goes through int() before it is stored. sum() on the resulting list is then real arithmetic.

This works because the file is simple. CSV allows a field to contain a comma if the field is wrapped in quotes, so a row like "Smith, Jo",70 is two fields: the name Smith, Jo and the mark 70. split(",") knows nothing about quotes and cuts it into three pieces - '"Smith', ' Jo"' and '70' - and every column after the name is now off by one. Nothing raises an error; the marks are simply wrong. The sibling program read-csv-module reads the same file with the csv module, which does understand the quoting rules.

To run this in PyCharm you need the data file too: make a folder called _fixtures next to the program and put a file scores.csv in it with these four lines - name,maths,physics,cs / Ada,91,78,95 / Brian,64,70,58 / Chen,88,92,81 (each / is a new line). The path _fixtures/scores.csv is relative, so it is looked up from the folder the program is run in, which is PyCharm's working directory, normally the program's own folder.
zh: 文件分两步读。readline() 单独拿走表头那一行，之后的 for 循环从文件当前所在的位置接着读，所以它只看到数据行。文件对象记得自己读到了哪儿，不需要在循环里再跳过表头。
每个字段读回来都是字符串，分数也不例外。"91" + "78" 得到的是 "9178"，所以每个分数存进去之前都过一遍 int()。之后对列表做 sum() 才是真正的算术。

它能用，是因为这份文件简单。CSV 允许字段里含逗号——只要用引号把这个字段括起来——所以 "Smith, Jo",70 这一行是两个字段：名字 Smith, Jo 与分数 70。split(",") 不认识引号，会把它切成三段：'"Smith'、' Jo"' 和 '70'，名字之后的每一列都错开一位。不会有任何报错，只是分数全错了。兄弟程序 read-csv-module 用 csv 模块读同一份文件，那个模块懂引号规则。

要在 PyCharm 里跑，还得有这份数据文件：在程序旁边建一个叫 _fixtures 的文件夹，里面放 scores.csv，内容四行——name,maths,physics,cs / Ada,91,78,95 / Brian,64,70,58 / Chen,88,92,81（每个 / 处换行）。_fixtures/scores.csv 是相对路径，从「程序在哪个文件夹里运行」开始找，也就是 PyCharm 的工作目录，通常就是程序自己所在的文件夹。

lineNotes.en: The loop starts after the header, because readline() on the line above already moved the file's position past it.
lineNotes.zh: 循环从表头之后开始，因为上一行的 readline() 已经把文件位置挪过了表头。

lineNotes.en: Two steps chained: drop the newline, then cut on commas. Without the first step the last field would be "95\n", and int() happens to tolerate that - but a text field in that position would silently keep the newline.
lineNotes.zh: 两步连写：先去掉换行，再按逗号切。少了第一步，最后一个字段会是 "95\n"；int() 碰巧能容忍它，但如果那一列是文字，换行符就会悄悄留在数据里。

lineNotes.en: Each row is stored as a tuple of (name, list of marks), which is what lets the main block unpack it as for name, marks in rows.
lineNotes.zh: 每行存成一个 (名字, 分数列表) 元组，所以主程序块才能写 for name, marks in rows 直接解包。

run.expect:
['name', 'maths', 'physics', 'cs']
Ada: [91, 78, 95] total 264
Brian: [64, 70, 58] total 192
Chen: [88, 92, 81] total 261

title.en: Read a CSV: the csv Module

blurb.en: The same file and the same output as the split version, with the parsing handed to the csv module.
blurb.zh: 同一份文件、同一份输出，只是把「切开」这件事交给了 csv 模块。

en: A csv reader wraps the open file and hands back each row already split into a list of strings, with the newline removed. It understands quoted fields, so "Smith, Jo",70 comes back as the two fields it really is. That is the whole reason to use it: the output here matches read-csv-split only because scores.csv contains no quotes.

The file is opened with newline set to the empty string. Normally Python translates line endings as it reads; the csv module wants to see the raw line endings itself, because a quoted field is allowed to contain a line break. The csv documentation asks for this on every file you hand to the csv module, reading or writing.

A reader is an iterator, the same kind of thing a file object is. The built-in next() takes one row out of it - the header - and the for loop continues from the row after. If the file were completely empty, next() would raise StopIteration, which is a loud failure rather than a silent wrong answer.
The values are still strings. The csv module splits text; it does not guess types, so the int() conversion is exactly the same as in the split version.

To run this in PyCharm you need the data file too: make a folder called _fixtures next to the program and put a file scores.csv in it with these four lines - name,maths,physics,cs / Ada,91,78,95 / Brian,64,70,58 / Chen,88,92,81 (each / is a new line). The path _fixtures/scores.csv is relative, so it is looked up from the folder the program is run in, which is PyCharm's working directory, normally the program's own folder.
zh: csv 读取器包住已打开的文件，每次交回一行已经切好的字符串列表，换行也已去掉。它懂带引号的字段，"Smith, Jo",70 读回来就是它真正的两个字段。用它的全部理由就在这里：本程序的输出与 read-csv-split 一样，只是因为 scores.csv 里恰好没有引号。
打开文件时把 newline 设成了空字符串。平常 Python 读文件时会翻译行尾；csv 模块要自己看到原始的行尾，因为带引号的字段里允许出现换行。csv 文档要求：交给 csv 模块的每个文件，读也好写也好，都这样打开。
读取器是一个迭代器，和文件对象是同一类东西。内置的 next() 从里面取出一行——表头——之后的 for 循环从下一行接着走。文件若完全是空的，next() 会抛 StopIteration：响亮地失败，而不是悄悄给出错答案。
值依然是字符串。csv 模块只管切，不猜类型，所以 int() 转换和 split 版一模一样。

要在 PyCharm 里跑，还得有这份数据文件：在程序旁边建一个叫 _fixtures 的文件夹，里面放 scores.csv，内容四行——name,maths,physics,cs / Ada,91,78,95 / Brian,64,70,58 / Chen,88,92,81（每个 / 处换行）。_fixtures/scores.csv 是相对路径，从「程序在哪个文件夹里运行」开始找，也就是 PyCharm 的工作目录，通常就是程序自己所在的文件夹。

lineNotes.en: Each fields is already a list like ['Ada', '91', '78', '95']: no rstrip, no split.
lineNotes.zh: 每个 fields 已经是 ['Ada', '91', '78', '95'] 这样的列表：不用 rstrip，也不用 split。

lineNotes.en: Part of the standard library, so nothing to install - it works the same in PyCharm as it does here.
lineNotes.zh: 标准库的一部分，无需安装——在 PyCharm 里和在这里一样能用。

run.expect:
['name', 'maths', 'physics', 'cs']
Ada: [91, 78, 95] total 264
Brian: [64, 70, 58] total 192
Chen: [88, 92, 81] total 261

title.zh: 用 DictWriter 与 DictReader 读写 CSV

blurb.en: Write records as dictionaries, look at the raw bytes that land in the file, and read them back - as strings.
blurb.zh: 把记录当字典写出去，看一眼真正落进文件的原始内容，再读回来——读回来的是字符串。

en: DictWriter maps dictionary keys to columns. fieldnames fixes the column order once, so it no longer matters what order the keys were typed in each dictionary. The header method writes the column names as the first row; forget it and the file has no header, and DictReader will then use your first data row as the column names.

Look at the repr of the file: every row ends in 
, not 
. The csv module always writes that line ending, which the CSV standard specifies. Open the file without newline set to the empty string and, on Windows, Python translates each 
 into 
 again, giving 
 - and a blank row appears between every record when the file is opened in Excel. That is why the newline argument appears on both opens.

DictReader gives back one dictionary per row, keyed by the header. Every value is a string: points went in as the int 12 and comes back as '12'. CSV has no types, only text, so int() is needed before any arithmetic - which is what the +1 in the last loop is for.
This program writes house_points.csv into the folder it runs in. Run it twice and the file is simply rewritten, because mode "w" empties it first.
zh: DictWriter 把字典的键对应到列。fieldnames 一次性定下列的顺序，于是每个字典里键是按什么顺序敲的就无所谓了。写表头的那个方法把列名写成第一行；忘了它，文件就没有表头，而 DictReader 会把你的第一行数据当成列名。

看文件的 repr：每行结尾是 
，不是 
。csv 模块总是写这种行尾，这是 CSV 标准规定的。打开时不把 newline 设成空字符串的话，在 Windows 上 Python 会把每个 
 再翻译成 
，得到 
——用 Excel 打开时每条记录之间都会多出一个空行。所以两处 open 都带着 newline 实参。
DictReader 每行交回一个字典，键来自表头。所有值都是字符串：points 写进去时是整数 12，读回来是 '12'。CSV 没有类型，只有文字，所以做算术前要 int()——最后那个循环里的 +1 就是为了让你看到这一点。
本程序会在运行它的文件夹里写出 house_points.csv。跑两次，文件只是被重写一遍，因为模式 "w" 会先把它清空。

lineNotes.en: One call per dictionary. writer.writerows(records) would do the whole list in one call; the loop is here so you can see that each record becomes one row.
lineNotes.zh: 每个字典调用一次。writer.writerows(records) 能一次写完整个列表；这里写成循环，是为了让你看清一条记录就是一行。

lineNotes.en: list() is needed here, not just tidy: the reader is lazy, and once the with block ends the file is closed, so rows that were not read yet could not be read at all.
lineNotes.zh: 这里的 list() 不是可有可无：读取器是惰性的，with 块一结束文件就关了，还没读的行就再也读不到了。

lineNotes.en: Note '12' in quotes: the value came back as a string.
lineNotes.zh: 注意 '12' 带着引号：这个值读回来是字符串。

blurb.en: Each of the four clauses prints its own name, so the output is the order they ran in - once without an error, once with one.
blurb.zh: 四个子句各自打印自己的名字，于是输出就是它们的执行顺序——一次没出错，一次出了错。

en: Read the two runs side by side. 10 / 4 raises nothing, so the except clause is skipped and else runs. 1 / 0 raises ZeroDivisionError on the division line; the rest of the try block is abandoned, the matching except runs, and else is skipped. In both runs finally runs, and then execution carries on after the whole statement.

else is for code that should run only when the try block succeeded. It could be written at the end of the try block instead, but then an exception of the same kind raised by that code would be caught by the except clause too, and blamed on the wrong line. Keeping the try block as short as the risky operation, and putting the follow-up in else, keeps the except honest.

finally is for clean-up that must happen whatever went on: closing something, printing a closing message, releasing a lock. leave_early shows the strongest case - the try block returns, and finally still runs before the value actually leaves the function. with closes a file for you on the same principle.

Only an exception that matches the except clause is caught. If a / b raised something else, such as TypeError, finally would still run, but the exception would then carry on out of divide() and stop the program.
zh: 把两次运行并排读。10 / 4 什么都不抛，所以跳过 except、执行 else。1 / 0 在除法那一行抛出 ZeroDivisionError；try 块剩下的部分被放弃，匹配的 except 执行，else 被跳过。两次运行里 finally 都执行，然后接着执行整个语句之后的代码。
else 放的是「只有 try 块成功了才该跑」的代码。它也可以写在 try 块末尾，但那样的话，这段代码自己抛出的同类异常也会被 except 接住、被算到错误的那一行头上。让 try 块只包住那个有风险的操作、把后续放进 else，except 才不会冤枉人。
finally 放的是无论发生什么都必须做的收尾：关掉某样东西、打印收尾信息、释放锁。leave_early 演示了最强的情形——try 块里直接 return，finally 依然在值真正离开函数之前执行。with 替你关文件，靠的也是同一个原理。
只有与 except 匹配的异常才会被接住。如果 a / b 抛的是别的，比如 TypeError，finally 依然执行，但异常随后会继续冲出 divide()，让程序停下。

lineNotes.en: The only line here that can raise. When it does, the print of the else clause is never reached, and result is set in the except clause instead.
lineNotes.zh: 这里唯一可能抛异常的一行。它一旦抛出，else 里的 print 就不会执行，result 改由 except 子句赋值。

lineNotes.en: The return value is decided here, but the function does not finish until finally has run - which is why the finally line prints before the value does.
lineNotes.zh: 返回值在这里就定下了，但函数要等 finally 跑完才真正结束——所以 finally 那行比返回值先打印出来。

run.expect:
try: 10 / 4
else: result is 2.5
finally: always runs
after the try statement
2.5
---
try: 1 / 0
except: cannot divide by zero
finally: always runs
after the try statement
None
---
finally: runs even on the way out of a return
value from try

blurb.en: One try block, four ways for it to go wrong, and a separate except clause for each - checked from the top down.
blurb.zh: 一个 try 块、四种出错方式、每种各有一个 except 子句——从上往下逐个比对。

en: When the try block raises, Python checks the except clauses in the order they are written and runs the first one that matches; the rest are ignored. Matching includes subclasses: an except for a class also catches every exception derived from it.

That is why the most specific clauses come first and Exception comes last. ZeroDivisionError, ValueError and TypeError are all subclasses of Exception, so if the Exception clause were at the top it would catch every one of them and the specific clauses below it could never run. Python does not warn you about an unreachable except clause.

as e binds the exception object to a name so you can use it. Printing it gives the message Python attached: for 'ten' that is invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'ten'. The ZeroDivisionError and TypeError clauses print their own wording instead, because they do not need anything from the exception object.

The last case passes None. None has no strip method, so the very first line of the try block raises AttributeError - a mistake none of the specific clauses expected. The catch-all reports it by class name. A catch-all is useful at the edge of a program, but it is also how real bugs get hidden, so it should always say what it caught rather than stay silent.
zh: try 块一抛异常，Python 就按书写顺序逐个检查 except 子句，执行第一个匹配的，其余全部忽略。「匹配」包括子类：接住一个类的子句，也接住从它派生出来的所有异常。
所以最具体的子句放前面，Exception 放最后。ZeroDivisionError、ValueError、TypeError 都是 Exception 的子类；要是 Exception 那个子句排在最上面，它会把这些统统接走，下面那些具体子句永远轮不到。Python 不会就「执行不到的 except」提醒你。
as e 把异常对象绑到一个名字上，好让你用它。打印它得到的是 Python 附上的消息：'ten' 对应的是 invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'ten'。ZeroDivisionError 与 TypeError 两个子句打印自己写的话，因为它们用不着异常对象里的任何东西。
最后一组传的是 None。None 没有 strip 方法，所以 try 块的第一行就抛出 AttributeError——哪个具体子句都没料到的错。兜底子句按类名把它报出来。兜底在程序的最外层很有用，但它也正是真 bug 被藏起来的地方，所以它应当总是说出自己接住了什么，而不是一声不吭。

lineNotes.en: Two things can go wrong on this line: text may not have a strip method at all (AttributeError), or the stripped text may not be a whole number (ValueError).
lineNotes.zh: 这一行可能出两种错：text 可能根本没有 strip 方法（AttributeError），或者去掉空格后的文字不是整数（ValueError）。

lineNotes.en: And two more here: divisor may be zero (ZeroDivisionError) or may be a string (TypeError).
lineNotes.zh: 这一行还有两种：divisor 可能是零（ZeroDivisionError），也可能是字符串（TypeError）。

run.expect:
' 12 ' / 4
  result: 3.0
'ten' / 2
  ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: 'ten'
  result: None
'7' / 0
  ZeroDivisionError: the divisor is zero
  result: None
'9' / '3'
  TypeError: the divisor is not a number
  result: None
None / 1
  something else: AttributeError
  result: None

title.zh: 输入不合法就 raise ValueError

blurb.en: The function refuses input it cannot handle by raising; the caller, which knows what the program is for, decides what happens next.
blurb.zh: 函数遇到处理不了的输入就 raise 拒绝；调用方知道程序是干什么的，由它决定接下来怎么办。

en: percentage() has no sensible answer when whole is zero or part is out of range. It could print a message and return None, but then every caller has to remember to check for None, and the one that forgets carries on with a wrong value. Raising ValueError makes the problem impossible to ignore: the caller either handles it or the program stops and says why.

raise ends the function immediately, like return does, but instead of handing back a value it sends an exception up to whoever called the function - and up again, until some try block catches it. That is why neither raise line needs an else after its if.

ValueError is the built-in exception for "the type is right but the value is not": an int was expected and an int arrived, just not one that makes sense here. TypeError would be the choice if the argument were the wrong type altogether. Pick the built-in that describes the problem before inventing your own exception class.
The message is part of the interface. The caller prints it, so it should say what was wrong in terms the reader of the output can act on - which is why the second message includes the actual numbers.
zh: whole 为零、或 part 超出范围时，percentage() 没有合理的答案。它可以打印一句话再返回 None，但那样每个调用方都得记得检查 None，而忘了检查的那个会带着一个错值继续跑。raise ValueError 让问题无法被忽视：调用方要么处理，要么程序停下并说明原因。
raise 和 return 一样立刻结束函数，但它交出去的不是值，而是把一个异常抛给调用这个函数的人——再往上抛，直到某个 try 块把它接住。所以两处 raise 所在的 if 后面都不需要 else。
ValueError 是「类型对、值不对」的内置异常：要的是 int、来的也是 int，只是在这里讲不通。如果实参干脆是错的类型，该用的是 TypeError。先找一个能描述问题的内置异常，再考虑自己造异常类。
消息是接口的一部分。调用方会把它打印出来，所以它要用读输出的人能据此行动的话说清哪里错了——这就是第二条消息里带上实际数字的原因。

lineNotes.at: raise ValueError(f"part {part} is not between 0 and {whole}")
lineNotes.en: An f-string message: the numbers that caused the problem go into the message, so the output says which input was rejected and why.
lineNotes.zh: 消息是 f-string：出问题的那几个数写进消息里，输出就能说清是哪个输入、为什么被拒。

lineNotes.en: Every rejection was handled, so the program reaches its last line. Remove the try and the first bad pair would stop it with a traceback instead.
lineNotes.zh: 每一次拒绝都被处理了，所以程序能走到最后一行。去掉 try，第一组坏数据就会让它带着 traceback 停下。

run.expect:
45/60 = 75.0%
rejected 70/60: part 70 is not between 0 and 60
rejected 3/0: whole must be positive
rejected -1/10: part -1 is not between 0 and 10
still running

blurb.en: A small family of exceptions for one module: a base class to catch them all, and a subclass that carries the numbers behind the error.
blurb.zh: 给一个模块造一小家子异常：一个基类用来一网打尽，一个子类身上带着出错时的那几个数。

en: An exception class is an ordinary class that inherits from Exception, directly or indirectly. BankError needs no body beyond its docstring - a docstring is enough to make a class body valid, just as pass is in AccountFrozen. What makes these useful is not their code but their names and their place in the hierarchy.

The hierarchy is the point. InsufficientFunds and AccountFrozen both inherit from BankError, so one except clause naming the base class catches either one, while a caller that only cares about one case can catch that subclass alone. A module that raises its own base class lets callers say "anything that went wrong with the bank" without also catching unrelated bugs, which catching Exception would do.

InsufficientFunds takes the balance and the amount and keeps them as attributes, so a caller can do arithmetic with them - short by 150 - instead of trying to pick numbers back out of the message string. super().__init__(message) passes the text up to Exception, which is what makes print(e) show it.
type(e).__name__ reads the class name off the exception object. In the loop the same except clause receives two different classes, and the output shows which one arrived each time.
zh: 异常类就是一个普通的类，直接或间接继承 Exception。BankError 除了文档串什么都不需要——文档串本身就足以让类体合法，和 AccountFrozen 里的 pass 作用相同。它们有用，不在于代码，而在于名字，以及在层次结构里的位置。
层次结构才是重点。InsufficientFunds 与 AccountFrozen 都继承 BankError，所以一个写基类的 except 子句两个都接得住；只关心其中一种情况的调用方，可以只接那个子类。模块抛自己的基类，调用方就能说「银行这边出的任何错」，而不会顺带把不相干的 bug 也接住——接 Exception 就会这样。
InsufficientFunds 收下余额与金额并存成属性，调用方可以直接拿来算——short by 150——而不必从消息字符串里把数字抠回来。super().__init__(message) 把文字交给 Exception，print(e) 能显示它，靠的就是这一句。
type(e).__name__ 从异常对象上读出类名。循环里同一个 except 子句先后收到两个不同的类，输出显示每次来的是哪一个。

lineNotes.en: Without this call the exception would still be raised and caught, but print(e) would show (100, 250) - the raw constructor arguments - instead of a sentence.
lineNotes.zh: 少了这一句，异常照样能抛、能接，但 print(e) 打出来的会是 (100, 250)——构造时的原始实参——而不是一句话。

lineNotes.en: Attributes on the exception, used as numbers. This is what a custom class gives you that a plain ValueError with a message does not.
lineNotes.zh: 异常对象上的属性，直接当数用。这正是自定义类能给、而一个只带消息的 ValueError 给不了的东西。

lineNotes.en: True, even though AccountFrozen never mentions Exception: it inherits from BankError, which does.
lineNotes.zh: True——尽管 AccountFrozen 从没提到 Exception：它继承的 BankError 提到了。

run.expect:
70
cannot withdraw 250 from 100
short by 150
InsufficientFunds -> cannot withdraw 50 from 20
AccountFrozen -> this account is frozen
True

title.en: Missing File: Try It and Catch
title.zh: 文件可能不在：先做再接

blurb.en: Open the file without checking first, and handle FileNotFoundError if it is not there - the Python habit called EAFP.
blurb.zh: 不先检查、直接打开文件，不在就处理 FileNotFoundError——Python 里叫 EAFP 的习惯。

en: EAFP stands for "easier to ask forgiveness than permission": do the thing, and deal with the failure if it happens. The open() call is the check. If the file is there you have already opened it; if it is not, the except clause runs. There is no moment in between where the answer could change.

The except clause names only the file-not-found exception, not OSError and not a bare except. A file that exists but cannot be read - no permission, or a folder with that name - raises a different exception, and hiding that behind "using defaults" would make a real problem look like a normal first run.

The exception object records which file it was about: filename holds the path exactly as it was passed to open(), and printing the exception gives the error number and the system's description. Both are relative here because the path was relative, which keeps the output the same on every computer.
Compare with missing-file-lbyl, which checks first. Both give the same first three lines of output.

To run this in PyCharm, make a folder called _fixtures next to the program with a file settings.txt in it holding two lines: volume=8 and theme=light. Leave no_such_file.txt out on purpose - its absence is the point.
zh: EAFP 是 "easier to ask forgiveness than permission"——先做，出了问题再收拾。open() 这个调用本身就是检查：文件在，你已经把它打开了；不在，就执行 except。中间不存在一个「答案可能又变了」的空档。
except 子句只写「文件不存在」那一种异常，不是 OSError，也不是裸 except。文件存在却读不了——没有权限，或者同名的其实是个文件夹——抛的是别的异常；用「改用默认值」把那种情况也盖过去，会让一个真问题看起来像一次普通的首次运行。
异常对象记着它说的是哪个文件：filename 就是传给 open() 的那个路径原样；打印异常本身得到错误号和系统的描述。这里两者都是相对的，因为路径本来就是相对路径——这样输出在每台电脑上都一样。
和先检查的 missing-file-lbyl 对照着看。两个程序输出的前三行完全相同。
要在 PyCharm 里跑：在程序旁边建一个 _fixtures 文件夹，里面放 settings.txt，两行：volume=8 和 theme=light。no_such_file.txt 故意不要建——它不存在，正是本程序要演示的。

lineNotes.en: splitlines() splits on line endings and drops them, so there is no trailing newline to strip and no empty string at the end.
lineNotes.zh: splitlines() 按行尾切开并把行尾去掉，所以不用再去换行，末尾也不会多出一个空字符串。

lineNotes.en: Deliberately not in a with block: this open() is expected to fail before there is any file to close.
lineNotes.zh: 故意没放进 with 块：这次 open() 预期会失败，根本不会有需要关闭的文件。

run.expect:
['volume=8', 'theme=light']
no_such_file.txt not found, using defaults
['volume=5', 'theme=dark']
no_such_file.txt | [Errno 2] No such file or directory: 'no_such_file.txt'

title.en: Missing File: Look Before You Leap
title.zh: 文件可能不在：先看再做

blurb.en: Ask pathlib whether the file exists before opening it - the same result as the try version, and the gap that approach leaves.
blurb.zh: 打开之前先问 pathlib 文件在不在——结果与 try 版相同，也看看这种做法留下的那道缝。

en: LBYL stands for "look before you leap": check that an operation can succeed, then do it. Path(path) turns the string into a path object, and exists() asks the file system whether anything is there. When it is not, the function returns the defaults and never calls open().

The check and the open are two separate moments. Between them another program could delete the file, and then open() raises FileNotFoundError anyway - with no except clause to catch it. On a single-user school project that almost never happens, but it is the reason Python code usually prefers the try version.

exists() answers a narrower question than it sounds. The last line shows it saying True for _fixtures, which is a folder. Pass a folder name to read_settings and exists() lets it through, then open() fails with IsADirectoryError (PermissionError on Windows). is_file() would be the stricter check. The try version has no such gap: it catches exactly the failure that occurred.
Where LBYL does read better is when the check is the point of the program - showing a message like "no save file yet, starting a new game" before anything else happens.

To run this in PyCharm, make a folder called _fixtures next to the program with a file settings.txt in it holding two lines: volume=8 and theme=light. Leave no_such_file.txt out on purpose - its absence is the point.
zh: LBYL 是 "look before you leap"——先确认操作能成功，再去做。Path(path) 把字符串变成路径对象，exists() 去问文件系统那里有没有东西。没有，函数就返回默认值，根本不调用 open()。
检查和打开是两个分开的时刻。两者之间别的程序可能把文件删掉，那时 open() 照样抛 FileNotFoundError——而这里没有 except 去接。一个人用的学校作业里这几乎不会发生，但这正是 Python 代码通常更偏爱 try 版的原因。

exists() 回答的问题比听上去要窄。最后一行显示它对 _fixtures 说 True，而那是个文件夹。把一个文件夹名交给 read_settings，exists() 会放行，接着 open() 失败，抛 IsADirectoryError（Windows 上是 PermissionError）。更严格的检查是 is_file()。try 版没有这道缝：它接住的恰好就是实际发生的那个失败。
LBYL 读起来更顺的场合，是「检查」本身就是程序要做的事——比如在一切开始之前先显示「还没有存档，开始新游戏」。
要在 PyCharm 里跑：在程序旁边建一个 _fixtures 文件夹，里面放 settings.txt，两行：volume=8 和 theme=light。no_such_file.txt 故意不要建——它不存在，正是本程序要演示的。

lineNotes.en: pathlib is in the standard library. Path objects work anywhere a string path does, including open().
lineNotes.zh: pathlib 在标准库里。Path 对象在任何能用字符串路径的地方都能用，open() 也包括在内。

lineNotes.en: True False True: it exists, it is not a file, it is a folder. exists() alone cannot tell those apart.
lineNotes.zh: True False True：存在、不是文件、是文件夹。只靠 exists() 分不出这几种。

run.expect:
['volume=8', 'theme=light']
no_such_file.txt not found, using defaults
['volume=5', 'theme=dark']
True False True

title.en: Keep Asking Until the Input Is Valid

blurb.en: A loop that only lets a whole number in range out - fed four bad answers before a good one.
blurb.zh: 一个只放行范围内整数的循环——先喂它四个坏答案，再给一个好的。

en: Two different things can be wrong with the answer, and they are checked in two different ways. Whether the text is a whole number at all is found out by trying int() and catching ValueError. Whether the number is in range is an ordinary if. Only when both pass does return end the loop - and the function.

continue jumps straight back to the top of the loop. Without it, after 'four' failed to convert, the program would go on to the range check with value never assigned, and crash with an error that has nothing to do with what the user typed.

int() is stricter and looser than you might guess. It accepts ' 4' with spaces around it, and a sign, but rejects '3.5' - a float in a string is not a whole number - and rejects the empty string you get when someone just presses Enter.

The demo feeds five lines through standard input: four, 3.5, an empty line, 0 and then 4. input() does not echo what it reads, so in the output each prompt is followed directly by the response to it. Typed at a real keyboard the answers would appear after the prompts.
zh: 答案可能错在两件不同的事上，用两种不同的方式查。文字到底是不是整数，靠「试着 int()、接住 ValueError」来发现；数字在不在范围里，是一个普通的 if。两关都过，return 才结束循环——也结束函数。
continue 直接跳回循环开头。没有它，'four' 转换失败之后程序会继续去做范围检查，而那时 value 根本没被赋值，于是崩在一个与用户输入毫不相干的错误上。
int() 比你以为的更严、也更松。它接受两边带空格的 ' 4'，也接受正负号；但拒绝 '3.5'——字符串里的小数不是整数——也拒绝别人直接按回车时得到的空字符串。
演示通过标准输入喂了五行：four、3.5、一个空行、0，然后是 4。input() 不回显读到的内容，所以输出里每个提示后面紧跟的是对它的回应。换成真键盘输入，答案会出现在提示之后。

lineNotes.en: Back to the top: ask again. This is the line that keeps a bad conversion from falling through to the range check.
lineNotes.zh: 回到开头，再问一次。正是这一行挡住了转换失败的情况，不让它漏到范围检查那里。

lineNotes.en: Reached only when the number converted but was out of range. No continue is needed here: this is already the last line of the loop body.
lineNotes.zh: 只有「转换成功但超出范围」才会走到这里。这里不需要 continue：它本来就是循环体的最后一行。

run.expect:
Rating 1-5: 'four' is not a whole number
Rating 1-5: '3.5' is not a whole number
Rating 1-5: '' is not a whole number
Rating 1-5: 0 is not between 1 and 5
Rating 1-5: Thanks, you gave it 4

blurb.en: Three ways to import, what each one puts in your file's namespace, and the if that decides whether the demo runs.
blurb.zh: 三种 import 写法、各自往你的文件里放进了什么名字，以及决定演示代码跑不跑的那个 if。

en: A plain import of math gives you one name, math, and everything is reached through it: math.floor. A from-import of sqrt gives you just the name sqrt, with no prefix and no access to anything else from math through it. Adding as to a plain import is the first form again, with a shorter name of your choosing - here, for statistics. The line sqrt is math.sqrt prints True: both names refer to the very same function object.

Prefer the plain import when you use several things from a module, because math.floor tells the reader where floor came from. from ... import is fine for one or two names used often. Avoid from math import * in real code: it pours every name into your file, and one of them may silently replace a name of your own.

Every file Python runs has a variable __name__. When the file is run directly - the Run button in PyCharm - it is set to "__main__". When another file imports it, __name__ is the module's name instead, as the math and stats lines show for those modules.

So the if at the bottom means: run the demo only when this file is the program, not when it is being used as a library. Without it, importing this file to reuse hypotenuse would also print everything below. Every program on these pages ends this way for exactly that reason.
zh: 普通地 import math，只给你一个名字 math，要用的东西都经由它取：math.floor。用 from 导入 sqrt，只给你 sqrt 这一个名字，不带前缀，也没法通过它拿到 math 里的其他东西。在普通 import 后面加 as，还是第一种写法，只是换成你自己取的短名字——这里给的是 statistics。sqrt is math.sqrt 打印 True：两个名字指向的是同一个函数对象。
要用一个模块里好几样东西时，优先用普通 import，因为 math.floor 让读代码的人知道 floor 从哪来。某一两个名字用得很频繁，用 from ... import 没问题。真正的代码里别写 from math import *：它把所有名字一股脑倒进你的文件，其中某一个可能悄悄顶掉你自己的名字。
Python 运行的每个文件都有一个变量 __name__。文件被直接运行时——PyCharm 里点 Run——它被设为 "__main__"。被别的文件 import 时，__name__ 则是模块名，math 与 stats 那两行显示的就是那两个模块的情形。
所以底部那个 if 的意思是：只有这个文件是「程序本身」时才跑演示，被当作库使用时不跑。没有它，别的文件为了复用 hypotenuse 而 import 这个文件时，下面那些 print 也会全部执行。这几页上的每个程序都这样收尾，理由就是这个。

lineNotes.en: sqrt with no prefix works only because of the from-import at the top. With just import math it would have to be math.sqrt.
lineNotes.zh: sqrt 不带前缀能用，全靠顶上那句 from-import。只有 import math 的话，这里得写 math.sqrt。

lineNotes.en: Prints __main__ here, because this file is being run directly. Imported from another file, the same line would print the module's name.
lineNotes.zh: 这里打印 __main__，因为本文件是被直接运行的。换成被别的文件 import，同一行会打印模块名。

run.expect:
5.0
2 5
True
this file: __main__
math module: math
stats alias: statistics
